overview: Global developments include House Republicans picking Jim Jordan as their next leader and new FDA warnings ordered for popular weight-loss drugs. In San Francisco, Mayor Lurie and the city administrator introduced new rules to fight corruption in the city's contracting system following voter-approved powers. Meanwhile, Honolulu’s affordable rental housing program has fallen short of its goals, according to a new report.

items.title: House Republicans Pick Jim Jordan, a Close Trump Ally, as Their Next Leader
items.summary: House Republicans chose Jim Jordan as their next leader over Representative Steve Scalise, signaling a desire for fresh leadership.

items.title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
items.summary: The US FDA ordered makers of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy to add warnings about a rare eye condition called NAION.

items.title: Honolulu’s Bill 7 housing program falling short of goals, report finds
items.summary: A University of Hawai‘i report found that Honolulu’s Bill 7 affordable rental housing program has produced only a fraction of its envisioned units.

items.title: Honolulu Council Sued Over Secret Zippy’s Meeting
items.summary: A lawsuit was filed against the Honolulu Council over a secret Zippy’s meeting, seeking to ban involved members from leadership positions.

items.title: Green Picks AG To Replace Lopez, Makes Other Cabinet Changes
items.summary: Governor Green appointed Matthew Dvonch as Hawaiʻi attorney general to replace Anne Lopez alongside other cabinet changes.

wiki.title: Regulus (Turner)
wiki.extract: Regulus is an oil painting by the English artist J. M. W. Turner, currently housed in Tate Britain, London. It was initially painted in 1828 and overpainted twice, first between 1829 and 1837, and again in 1837. The painting is based on a legend about the Roman consul and general Marcus Atilius Regulus, in which he was captured by Carthaginian forces and executed after refusing a prisoner exchange. Many accounts add that he was tortured by being forced to stare at the sun, blinding him. The painting depicts a harbour in either Rome or Carthage, with ships and buildings surrounding the ocean. It is dominated by the large white sun in the centre.
